name: Mauve grey
lede: Mauve grey is a muted, greyed violet-pink, one of several modifiers built on the flower name [[mauve]], first charted by Ridgway in 1912 and picked up again in the ISCC-NBS system in 1955.

sections.title: A grey cousin of mauve
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 color nomenclature lists this tone, and the ISCC-NBS system revisited it in 1955, placing it in block 228, the "pale purple" region, about 5.3 units from that block's own center color [1]. The 29 color books held in color-kb do not mention Mauve grey by name [4].

In the ColorHub library the same point is also carried under Vinaceous-Grey, an exact duplicate name (ΔE 0.0) rather than a separate shade [1][3]. Its closest distinct neighbor is [[irisglow]], 2.8 units away and described in our graph as "almost the same" [3]. Both sit a step greyer and cooler than plain [[mauve]], which the name modifies [1].

The word mauve itself comes from the French name for the mallow flower, borrowed into English after William Perkin's 1856 dye made the color fashionable [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this tone in 246 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.0 percent, as photographed [2]. It is not common before the twentieth century: its presence roughly triples in paintings from the 1900s onward, and peaks in the 1910s, in 22 of 523 paintings [2]. Counts are computed color matches on varnished, photographed canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
